title: No source publishes the four consumed surfaces the pack step needs: the pack and defect-list read of rwb-document, the notice and template-status read of rwb-comms, the case read with its task raise and route fact of rwb-case, and the D7 approval item of rwb-decision
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 sections 3 (Depends on FEAT-LIT-05), 4 (Endpoints), 12 (in-process calls) and 11 (Data: document, notice, recovery_case, task, timer, decision_log_entry); FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A2.7.2 (Integration points: Workbench), A2.7.3.1 (VR-S4-007-1, R-LIT-04, R-LIT-11, R-LIT-16) and the screens and requirements blocks; TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T5.2 (calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices), T5.3 (events: None), T-A.1 (five operations, one of them first in E2) and T3.1; _work/msr/context/S4.md ownership rows (5 REST operations provided, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13, R7.2 s12
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 2, 3, 8 and 10; 5 Exception paths X9 and X10; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC3; 8 Business rules BR3, BR4 and BR5; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.5; 12.8; 13 Solution plan Components and Build steps 2 to 5; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the consumed surface of the application slice. (1) The legacy step read the pack, the notice, the case and the task it raised through in-process Java calls against one recovery schema, and wrote the decision log entry beside them. No source names a consumer-facing REST operation for any of the four answers, nor a path, a page shape or an error mapping. (2) TSD S4 T5.2 names the owners (P3, P7, P5, P6) and calls them published Java interfaces, which the target replaces with contract-first REST (DP-11); the ownership rows of rwb-litigation give it five provided operations and no consumed one. (3) The D7 approval item of R-LIT-11 is the same case: RWB-P7-E2013-CON is named in the sibling stories as the approval contract, but the operation that raises an item is published by no source. (4) The reference data of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS is DP-07 and not in this key's pattern set, so its read carries no row either. (5) The four rows are therefore declared as answers with the placeholder, faked, and one hop with a 2 s budget.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 3: 'Depends on FEAT-LIT-05'; section 4 lists only POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve and POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions; section 11 names recovery_case, task, timer, legal_action, notice and decision_log_entry as the story's data; TSD S4 v2 T5.2: 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'; TSD S4 v2 T5.3: 'Events: None'; _work/msr/context/S4.md gives rwb-litigation 5 REST operations provided and 0 events.
proposed: Publish the four answers on their owners' bases as part of the wave 3 contract freeze: a pack and defect-list read on rwb-document, a notice and template-status read on rwb-comms, a case read with the route fact and the task raise on rwb-case, and the approval raise of RWB-P7-E2013-CON on rwb-decision, each answering the elements the app story names in 12.2, each one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, each with a fake; add the reference-data read of RWB-P3-E1043-CON to the same freeze; until they publish, the app story builds against the fakes of its contract.

title: The legacy data block and endpoint block give this story the case, the task, the timer, the notice and the decision ledger, which the target assigns to rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-decision
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 11 Data (recovery_case, task, timer, legal_action, notice, decision_log_entry) and section 4 Endpoints (POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve, Litigation A; POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, Litigation C); _work/msr/context/S4.md ownership rows (tables: hearing, legal_action only; 5 REST operations provided, one of them the notice approve); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action and hearing only), T4 (the 38 litigation states), T6.1; Architecture v5 slides 3 and 4 (P3 case and workflow, P6 communications, P7 decision); FSD S4 v3 existing capability check (case record and shared entities read through the P3 interfaces; workflow and state machine from P3; notification path reused); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11, R7.2 s12
section: 1 Story; 4 Flow steps 1, 8 and 10; 8 Business rules BR3 and BR5; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.7; 13 Solution plan Components; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the ownership disagreement. (1) The legacy data block gives the story recovery_case, task, timer, notice and decision_log_entry as its own tables; the Ownership Map gives S4 two tables, hearing and legal_action, and the TSD defines only those two. (2) The litigation states of TSD S4 T4 (NOTICE_GENERATED, NOTICE_BLOCKED, NOTICE_UNSERVED, PACK_ASSEMBLY, PACK_VERIFIED, FIRM_SELECTION) are described in the TSD as the litigation state machine, while the target makes each a route state of the case of record in rwb-case, moved on a fact the route service announces. (3) The legacy endpoint block gives the story the notice approval operation, which the TSD places first in E2 and which the ownership rows still list as an operation of rwb-litigation whose business effect belongs to the notices.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 11 lists 'recovery_case, task, timer, legal_action, notice, decision_log_entry' with BR Field IDs DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023, DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-036, DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-023 and DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; section 4 lists POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve; _work/msr/context/S4.md tables: hearing, legal_action; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines legal_action and hearing only; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 marks API-S4-001 'First in: E2'; FSD S4 v3 existing capability check: 'Case record and shared entities - REUSE - Read through the P3 interfaces'.
proposed: Keep the split of the ownership rows: rwb-litigation writes legal_action and the library objects only, rwb-case owns the case, its route states, the task and the timers, rwb-comms owns the notice and its template, and rwb-decision owns the ledger and the approval item. Let the app story announce each litigation fact as a route fact and accept the answer, and let the notice approval operation stay with the E2 notice story; record the two legacy blocks as Outdated in the Change Register.

title: No stored field or list value carries the pack verification, the filing authorisation, the defect-list result, the template status or the prescription days, and no status value names the two acts
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 7 (AC1 confirm the pack and authorize the filing), 11 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014; no pack, checklist or approval field) and 15 (SCR-19 states pack, instructed, filed, hearing, judgment); FSD S4 v3 A2.7.3.1 (R-LIT-16 condition every defect list item present; R-LIT-23 condition pack_verified_at set), A2.7.3.2 (field catalog: 8 fields, none of them a verification or an approval), A2.7 metric (litigation turnaround 6 days measured on the decision log and Workbench records); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (14 legal_action columns), T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-STATUS: OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN), T3.0; _work/msr/context/S4.md tables (hearing, legal_action); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-11 condition prescription_days_remaining <= 90; R-LIT-16 every defect list item present)
section: 1 Story; 5 Exception paths X4 to X6; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC3; 8 Business rules BR1 and BR6; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.7; 13 Solution Base and Configuration; 16 Test cases
description: One combined row for the data model of the pack step. (1) R-LIT-16 needs every defect list item present, R-LIT-23 needs pack_verified_at set, R-LIT-04 needs a template status of withdrawn and R-LIT-11 needs prescription_days_remaining; legal_action has fourteen columns and none of them holds any of the four facts, and S4 owns no other table that does. (2) No value of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS names a verified pack or an authorised filing, so the two acts of AC1 cannot be published as a status. (3) The defect list, its rows and its version are held by no source read for this key; the checks are named and their content is not. (4) The 90-day threshold is stated by R-LIT-11 and by no configuration source.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 legal_action: DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 (id, case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name, claim_amount, filed_date, judgment_date, judgment_amount, lit_status, status); T3.2 LOV-LEGAL-STATUS has six values and none of them names a verification or an authorisation; FSD S4 A2.7.3.2 field catalog lists 8 fields and no pack or approval field; FSD S4 A2.7.3.1 R-LIT-16 'every defect list item present'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-23 'pack_verified_at set' and R-LIT-11 'prescription_days_remaining <= 90'.
proposed: Keep legal_action as TSD S4 T3.1 defines it and store neither the verification nor the authorisation on the row: let both live on the decision record of DP-03 and on the case route state of rwb-case, and let the row keep OPEN until a filing date is written. Publish the two acts as the contract elements of RWB-S4-E5007-CON rather than as status values, and read the defect list, the template status and the prescription days on the owners' contracts. Record the checklist rows and the 90-day row as versioned reference data of the business to be supplied before the wave 3 build.

title: No source fixes how the template-withdrawn fact and the prescription warning reach the service, or who owns the 1-working-day and 2-working-day service levels of R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-16
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 AC2 and AC3, section 11 (task, timer), section 15 (SCR-18 states generated to unserved); FSD S4 v3 A2.3.2 (Integration points: Workbench, Quartz scheduler), A2.7.2 (Integration points: Workbench), A2.7.4.4 and A2.4.4.4 (System background events: None), A2.7.1 (metric measured on the decision log and Workbench records); TSD S4 v2 T5.3 (Events: None), T4 (R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-11 rows), T5.1 (INT-33 as entered); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04 (service level 1 working day), R-LIT-11 (to the prescription date), R-LIT-16 (2 working days); _work/msr/context/S4.md (0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09, DP-10 and DP-14
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 5, 8 and 10; 5 Exception paths X5 and X11; 8 Business rules R-LIT-04, R-LIT-11 and R-LIT-16; 9 State transitions; 12.4; 12.5; 12.6; 13 Solution plan Configuration
description: One combined row for the delivery and the timing. (1) The template withdrawal of R-LIT-04 and the prescription warning of R-LIT-11 are events of the rule table, and the FSD declares no background event for the feature and the TSD declares no event of the service; DP-09 and DP-10 are not in this key's pattern set, so the service subscribes to no topic and registers no Schedule. (2) The legacy story raised a task and held a timer in its own schema; in the target the task and the timer are the case of record's and no source says which contract raises them or answers them. (3) The 1-working-day service level of R-LIT-04, the 2-working-day level of R-LIT-16 and the to-the-prescription-date level of R-LIT-11 have no owner: they are durable timers of a workflow no source assigns.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.7.4.4: 'None - No background event'; TSD S4 v2 T5.3: 'None'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04 service level '1 working day', R-LIT-16 '2 working days', R-LIT-11 'To the prescription date'; _work/msr/context/S4.md: 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow; FSD S4 v3 A2.3.2 integration points 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' against R-LIT-11.
proposed: Read both facts synchronously: the template status on the rwb-comms answer and the prescription date and days remaining on the rwb-case answer, with no topic, no consumer and no Schedule in this service. Leave the task raise, the timers and the three service levels with rwb-case and with the approval child workflow of rwb-decision, and record the assignment in the run summary so that the case stories and the decision stories carry the clocks.

title: The legacy story and the Epics 3 to 8 specification carry no requirement identifier for this feature
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 metadata block (Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on, Decision only); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md line 51 (the E5 S4 row for FEAT-LIT-07 with no REQ column); FSD S4 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010); TSD S4 v2 T8 (requirement traceability written one epic ahead)
description: One row for the traceability of the key. The legacy story master of RWB-E5-007 has no REQ identifier and the Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the E5 S4 row without one, while the FSD serves REQ-S4-003 for verifying the pack before filing is approved and REQ-S4-009 for prescription warnings. The story therefore traces to REQ-S4-003 and to FEAT-LIT-07 until the PRD adds the identifiers.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-007 metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on, Decision; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md line 51: 'E5 | S4 | FEAT-LIT-07 | Verify the pack and approve filing | User | ... | Litigation officer | Workbench | FEAT-LIT-05'; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served: REQ-S4-003 'The litigation officer verifies the pack against the defect list before filing is approved'.
proposed: Trace the legacy key to REQ-S4-003 and FEAT-LIT-07 in the RTM and in both stories of the key, and let the Epics 3 to 8 PRD add the requirement identifiers for the feature; no new requirement is invented here.

(1) The TSD names the operations and three request or answer types and gives no property list for the pack verification, the filing authorisation, the case route fact or the task raise; the FSD field catalog covers the legal action only. title: The legacy endpoint block gives the contract the notice approval operation, which the TSD places first in Epic 2 and which the ownership rows still list under rwb-litigation
source: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 4 Endpoints (POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve, Litigation A; POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, Litigation C) and section 15 (SCR-18 Notice approval, first in E2); TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 (API-S4-001 first in E2) and T-A.2 (purpose: approve a generated notice for dispatch); _work/msr/context/S4.md REST operations provided (POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve); FSD S4 v3 screens block (SCR-18 first in E2); Architecture v5 slide 4 (P6 communications); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and R5.7 rule 1
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 5 Exception paths X6; 7 Acceptance criteria AC7; 8 Business rules BR11; 12.1; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the two facts of the key that were already built or belong to another story. (1) The legacy endpoint block of RWB-E5-007 names the notice approval operation with Litigation right A; the TSD marks that operation as first delivered in E2, so the notice half of the word approve was built an epic before this key and its business effect belongs to the notice story. (2) The ownership rows still list the operation under rwb-litigation, so a reader can mistake it for a provided operation of this baseline. (3) The D7 approval item this key consumes is RWB-P7-E2013-CON and carries no contract-dependency row in the plan, which is recorded with CG-B2-S4-007-1.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-007 section 4: 'POST | /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve | Litigation A'; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1: 'API-S4-001 | POST | /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve | Litigation A | E2'; _work/msr/context/S4.md lists POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve among the 5 operations provided.
proposed: Declare the notice approval operation out of this baseline and keep it with the E2 notice story that already serves it, while rwb-litigation keeps it in its published surface; fix in the baseline that the pack step approves no notice and that R-LIT-04 only blocks the generation. Record the E2 delivery in the Change Register so that a later reader does not reopen the key for a notice approval.
